subject: Clarify: processing footprint, subprocessors, and transfer hops
messages:
From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@clearhaven.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Data residency and transfer hops — quick clarifications

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. As part of our security review we need a concise picture of exactly where ClearHaven customer requests and model inference are processed and which third‑party subprocessors see or touch request data. Specifics we need:

- Primary regions where inference executes (for text/chat requests and embeddings).
- Any cross‑border hops (e.g., request enters US region then forwarded to EU/Asia for batching or model shards).
- Subprocessors that might store logs, metrics, or temporary caches and the logical purpose (metrics, storage, model hosting, etc.).
- Retention/deletion guarantees for logs/metadata and whether we can request account‑level deletion.

If you have a one‑pager, map, or CSV of subprocessors that would be ideal. We’re aiming to close the security questionnaire by EOD Friday so appreciate a timely reply.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Ruiz
Head of Security
ClearHaven AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@clearhaven.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 18:41:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency and transfer hops — quick clarifications

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a short processing map (redwood_processing_map_v1.pdf) and our current subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_20280610.csv) — both are the most up‑to‑date artifacts we share with prospects. High level summary here:

- Primary execution regions: US (us‑west1, us‑east1) for hosted customers by default. We also operate EU (europe‑west1) and APAC (asia‑east1) regions; customers can pin to a region on Dedicated/Private.
- Cross‑border hops: For hosted accounts on our multi‑region pool, live inference runs in the configured region. Non‑pinned requests may be routed for capacity/failover — we list those typical hops in the attached map.
- Subprocessors: roster lists compute partners, logging (metrics) provider, and content delivery/caching layers. Not all subprocessors see plaintext model inputs — we call this out in the CSV.
- Retention & deletion: short answer — we retain request logs/metadata for up to 30 days by default; customers can opt for shorter retention or request on‑demand deletion for account data. We provide deletion evidence for account deletion requests (audit log entries).

I’ll loop in Hannah (security) and Rishi (infra) to provide a technical breakdown and to answer any specific questions about KV cache and key management.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_processing_map_v1.pdf (processing map, 1 page), subprocessor_roster_20280610.csv (CSV, 3 cols)

From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@clearhaven.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 09:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency and transfer hops — quick clarifications

Thanks Marissa — the docs help. Couple of follow‑ups from our team:

1) For a request that hits our app (US region pinned) — is there any case under normal operation where tokens or KV cache are routed to a different region for batching or model sharding?
2) Do any subprocessors in the roster have access to user‑level request content (not just telemetry)? Which ones, and why?
3) For deletion evidence — what does the audit trail look like and how quickly can we get proof after an account deletion request?

We may need a short tech call (20–30m) to close these items. Can Hannah or Rishi join?

—Daniel

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@clearhaven.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jun 2028 15:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency and transfer hops — quick clarifications

Hi Daniel — looping in Hannah (Security) and Rishi (Infra) for the technical answers. Below is a concise breakdown; I asked them to confirm specifics and link any evidence artifacts.

Hannah / Rishi: please see Daniel’s three questions above — replied inline.

1) Cross‑region KV/cache routing:
- Normal operation (customer pinned to US region): inference, KV cache, and short‑term request caches remain within the pinned region.
- Exceptions: automatic failover/overflow — if the pinned region is saturated and the customer has allowed cross‑region failover, requests may be routed to an alternate region for short durations. We mark these events in the routing logs and surface them via the Console.
- Batching & sharding: model serving is co‑located with the sequence execution for LLM inference; we do not split a single request across multiple regions. Large offline batch jobs (model tuning, evaluation) may run in other regions but these are separate from live inference.

2) Subprocessor access to request content:
- Our roster categorizes subprocessors by access level: (A) plaintext access (model hosts or GPU cloud providers that run inference), (B) metadata/telemetry only (metrics, observability providers), (C) encrypted/managed storage (backups, object storage with server‑side encryption). See attached CSV column "access_level" for each vendor.
- Short list of vendors that may see plaintext inputs: primary cloud GPU hosts for hosted customers when running in those regions (names in CSV). For Dedicated/Private customers, you can request contractual controls and isolation so that only your pinned hosts run your traffic.

3) Deletion evidence & timing:
- Account deletion or data purge: once a formal deletion request is submitted via the Console or signed request, we execute the purge across services and produce an audit bundle containing: routing logs, deletion job id, affected object ids, and confirmation timestamps.
- SLA: standard turnaround for evidence bundle is 72 hours for hosted accounts. For Dedicated/Private, we can agree shorter windows in contract.

Evidence links & attachments provided:
- subprocessor_roster_20280610.csv (attached): vendor, region, access_level, purpose, contract link column.
- redwood_processing_map_v1.pdf (attached): high‑level diagram showing how requests move between frontdoor, routing, serving, and caching layers.
- Drive folder with SOC 2 and subprocessor contracts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c3-redwood-evidence

If helpful, we can schedule a 20m call — I’ve proposed two slots below. Hannah / Rishi, please add any clarifications or call availability.

Proposed call slots (US‑friendly):
- Thu 14 Jun, 16:00–16:20 UTC
- Fri 15 Jun, 15:00–15:20 UTC

Thanks,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Ruiz <daniel.ruiz@clearhaven.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 18:26:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data residency and transfer hops — quick clarifications

Marissa / team — thanks, that addresses most of our questions. A couple final notes:

- ClearHaven will accept hosted in us‑west but we need the 72h deletion evidence SLA in writing.
- Can you confirm that overflow routing will appear in the Console with timestamps and that we can pull routing logs for a given time window?

If all good, let’s set the Fri 15 Jun, 15:00 UTC call to finalize and sign the mutual action plan. I’ll have our procurement lead (emma.holt@clearhaven.ai) on the call.
